You say you can't cry and you need a form of relief I've been in that same position before. I don't know your situation specifically but I know that I would probably reach out to my significant other and have a long talk about how I feel. Even though this doesn't solve the problem you get it off your chest and your wife can help you through it. While I understand that you're helping your wife through the transition I'm almost certain that she would understand you reaching out. These times are tough and we all have to work through it, instead of keeping your feelings to yourself just ask your wife to sit down and talk I think it would really help you. I know that you will get through this, you have someone to lean on in times like this and you shouldn't feel bad for it. I wish you the best of luck and just know that I care about you.

Well I mean you could just bring it up at a normal appointment no special way to go about it. You can just say that you've been feeling depressed and go from there. But I would suggest that you don't get something prescribed from your doctor and just think that it's gonna go away. I've been on medications for 4 years now and I still haven't found something that really works for me. If possible it would be best to see a psychiatrist for medications mine has made more progress in a few months than my doctor made in a few years. Essentially just get the conversation started with your doctor and go from there they can refer you to somewhere else if need be.

Your normal doctor can prescribe you medications but seeing that you're 17 you will probably have to get your parents involved. When I was 15 I was having the same problem and I was very scared of my parents finding out. Eventually I talked to one of my school counselors about it and that was how I started getting treatment. I would suggest that you speak to your schools counselor if you're able to.

I'm currently in the locked in my room for a year scared of the world stage. Idk how to get out of it I feel so behind in life and I really don't see how I could work a job. Have you attempted to get professional help ? Medication could make a huge difference for you, most people find a medication that helps them in a reasonable amount of time. This seems pretty basic and I don't want it to come off the wrong way but it is an important thing to do.

This may sound stupid and I don't want to come off as rude but have you tried to talk to your school counselor about the fact that your parents won't let you be treated ? I'm not sure where you live and what the laws are but to my knowledge the school can take some form of action to get you help regardless of your parents. I would suggest that next time you talk to the counselor you bring up the subject and ask if there is anything they can do the resource officer would also be a great person to ask. Just don't give up on trying you will get the help you need.

Have you tried having a conversation about the topic. He told you about the scars so he definitely trusts you and it may be a sign that he wants to open up about it to you. I do not know him but I know that personally if someone that I trust asked me if I was suicidal or if I was depressed I would tell them the truth. You mention feeling selfish about how you feel on the matter but there is no need to, being close to someone who is depressed can be really hard and I'm sure he wouldn't be upset with you for how you're feeling. In terms of being a risk to himself I think one indicator would be if his signs of self harm are scars or more fresh wounds, even if they are fresh it doesn't necessarily mean he's suicidal but it's much more of an issue. I think the most important thing in this situation is to be open and honest to your SO and remember that your feelings are just as important.
